quotes.text: Make no mistake about it, Currents, like every album Don released before it (or even after it, for that matter) is a very good album.
The album opens up with a Hugh Prestwood song, "Only Water (Shining In The Air)", mid-tempo ballad with a little different sound than previous efforts
"Too Much Love" has a sing-a-long quality to it and, again, a little more of a contemporary sound to it.

Penned by Charles John Quarto and Steve Gillette, the song is a slow ballad that sounds like a typical late 60s – early 70s production with steel guitar and (to a lesser degree) harmonica very prominent in the arrangement.
This mid-tempo ballad also features mid-70s country production.
"In The Family" features a Caribbean rhythm verging on reggae. It's different but it works
Like most Don Williams recording, this is taken at a relaxed tempo, but it tells a complete story and probably would have been a bigger hit had there been a major label pushing it forward.
Don Williams mostly stayed away from the barroom songs.
Don Williams is one of the few artists that can stay in a slow groove forever, without it becoming boring
Don Williams Volume One is a really fine album that I frequently revisit. It contains solid country production, well written songs sung with honest but not overwrought emotion.
Williams reunites with the studio producer that helped him gain 17 #1 songs helped shaped his mellow, easy-going Country sound during his heyday with MCA and Capitol Records Garth Fundis.
It fits like it's supposed to without pretense. It would be wrong, nay sacrilege for Don to go where Country music has gone today…which is pretty much downhill and in the gutter.
Today's Country is so far removed from this beautiful sound that strings are frowned upon. Thank God Don knows his voice and his audience!
It has that familiar easy-going trot with backing strings and percussion that are "the Gentle Giant's" trademark sound.
Don is a natural without hyperbole, pretense or haughtiness. His understated vocals hit the tone just right and make you want to listen to it over and over again.
